# Read this first

## Funded Sandbox checkout settlement, search indexing allowlist — 2026-11-07

- Hosted checkout now prints a `checkout:<token>` Sandbox destination. A
  developer Sandbox wallet looks it up, locks the amount to the session's exact
  satoshis and pays it: payer debit, merchant credit, `simulation_paid`,
  `paid_via: "sandbox_transfer"`, merchant "Received" receipt and signed webhook
  are written through a durable three-phase settlement that is idempotent and
  resumed by the next request or the dispatcher sweep. Refused credits (expired,
  already paid, limits) release the debit with a 409 reason. The hosted page
  prints the receipt terminal inline, then returns to the merchant after 14 s.
  Manual "Mark paid manually" remains as a console fallback.
- Documentation and starter guidance now state why a forged webhook cannot mark
  an order paid (HMAC with shared secret, timestamp window, event-id dedupe,
  order binding, authenticated GET confirmation). The server never trusted the
  browser; no public route can set `paid_at`.
- Indexing: the shell no longer carries a global noindex meta. The API server
  serves `/robots.txt` (allowlist: `/`, `/developers`, `/developers/about`,
  `/developers/apply`, `/developers/resources` and its six section paths, plus
  `/assets/`) and `/sitemap.xml` from `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`; `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`
  stays on every other path, and the web app sets per-route title, description,
  canonical and robots meta. New public pages: `/developers/about` and
  `/developers/resources/<section>`. Owner vault, console, Sandbox, hosted
  checkout and admin routes remain non-indexable by header, robots and meta.
- External integrator feedback (ConnectLive sandbox test, 7/10) addressed:
  return-URL completion parameters (`checkout_id`, `status`) documented; the
  three completion paths (Sandbox wallet, test-key API, console fallback) laid
  out in one place; new bearer endpoint
  `POST /api/v1/checkout/sessions/:id/simulate` for automated tests (Sandbox
  only, same semantics and limits as the console action, OpenAPI + unit test);
  a chapter listing the Live behaviours that are not yet defined
  (confirmations, under/overpayment, expiry funds, refunds, fees, settlement).
  Their remaining items (public webhook endpoint, real-money detection) are on
  the merchant side or blocked on Live activation.
- Platform-admin `configured:false` remains unresolved (runtime secret value).
  No deployment, host change, real transfer or Git push occurred.

This is the living project reference. It describes the repository, not a claim
that every implemented feature has passed live commissioning. It is an R Markdown
document containing ordinary Markdown; reading it requires no R runtime. Optional
HTML rendering requires R and rmarkdown, which are not required by the application.

**Live is mainnet-only in source; hosted custody is not yet verified ready.**
Owner screenshots show the separate mainnet Core and engine running with retained
mainnet storage. Signet remains stopped by the owner's explicit choice; Sandbox
simulation is not an on-chain Signet wallet. Actual deployed website runtime
variables, mainnet sync completion and receive/send readiness require separate
verification. A running deployment, a QR code, a successful build and a healthy
node do not establish real-money custody readiness.

Evidence labels used here:

- **Source:** implemented or configured in the repository.
- **Local check:** a local validation result, not proof of the deployed environment.
- **Owner-confirmed:** reported by the owner, not independently repeated by an agent.
- **Screenshot:** visible in supplied screenshots; a point-in-time observation.
- **Pending:** not established by the available evidence.

## Owner administration and Sandbox checkout (2026-10-28)

**Source:** `/admin` reuses owner authentication and requires recent passkey
confirmation for writes. Account freeze/suspend, API/session revocation,
simulation credit/debit, pause/resume, application review and audit are wired.
Adjustments carry idempotent request IDs. Approval does not enable live custody.

`/developers/checkout` provides exact return-URL settings, encrypted webhook
secret rotation, checkout-only hashed `sk_test_` keys, preview creation, explicit
simulation and delivery history/retry. `/checkout/:token` is public status-only.
Its branded QR encodes the checkout URL, **not a Bitcoin deposit address**.
“I've sent” cannot mark paid; receipt simulation requires the authenticated
merchant. The customer returns to an allowlisted URL only after simulated receipt.
Python/Node examples use `/api/v1/checkout/sessions`; HTML calls the merchant's
own server, never embeds the key.

**Local HTTP evidence:** checkout creation/reconciliation, conflicting idempotency
keys, cross-tenant denial, public check non-mutation, concurrent simulation,
encrypted outbox, webhook lease, admin passkey gate, freeze/pause/suspend,
adjustment reconciliation and disabled Live approval are covered by local tests.
The injected delivery transport is not evidence of public HTTPS webhook delivery.

**Storage/operations:** `developer_control` is additive schema version 3.
Account CAS writes atomically record simulated receipt and durable webhook event.
API-owned delivery sweeps use leases, bounded retries, encrypted signing keys and
public-IPv4 HTTPS-only requests with pinned DNS resolution. No R2/Worker/queue
deployment or hosted database migration was performed. See
`docs/sandbox-checkout.md` for detailed limits and operational semantics.

Schema version 4 adds append-only `developer_security_audit`, separate from
developer-controlled history limits. Emergency owner revoke/suspend records
requested/applied events without appending to the full tenant history. Regression
coverage fills ordinary audit to 2,000 records, confirms ordinary writes stop,
then confirms both owner actions still remove sessions/keys and preserve history.
Admin views show recent history only; older security rows are retained, not purged.

**Not established:** authenticated responsive browser acceptance, real-device
passkeys, hosted mail/webhook delivery, production-wide throttling and backup
restore. The prior stalled browser run is not a pass. The public homepage cutover
remains disabled pending its acceptance gate. Existing owner routing is intact,
Signet is paused and Live custody is disabled. This is not a production launch.

one simulated receipt. Those records are partial evidence only: rotation,
cross-tenant browser behavior, expiry/cache clearing, lost-response UI recovery,
owner-prefixed navigation and tablet/desktop acceptance are **not certified**.
The root-homepage switch remains OFF until the release gate is completed. The
owner homepage remains at `/`; `/developers` is available separately. Do not
mark this foundation as publicly launched or fully accepted.

Single-owner, self-hosted Bitcoin vault with a responsive web interface. The
project uses React/TypeScript and Node.js/Express for the website and API, and Go
for the private Bitcoin engine. C# is not part of the current implementation.
AWS is the host for Coolify, not an application integration with AWS managed
services. Cloudflare D1 remains the production metadata store.

The interface includes a portfolio overview, cold and spending wallets, temporary
receiving wallets, receiving QR codes, transactions, payment review, node explorer,
market/alerts and operational settings. The explorer uses the owner's node rather
than requiring a public block explorer. The existence of a screen does not mean
its external service is configured.

## Owner requirements

- No username/password account system: use a manually saved random owner key and
  enrolled passkeys.
- Owner credential is 64 random bytes encoded as 86 unpadded base64url characters.
  Its SHA-256 verifier is 64 hexadecimal characters. These lengths describe
  different encodings/objects; they are not interchangeable credentials.
- Support many independent temporary receiving wallets; the batch UI supports up
  to 200 per request. Local regtest evidence includes 101 wallets; live scale
  readiness remains separate.
- Show timestamps, incoming transactions, pending/confirmed balances, and expiry.
- Temporary wallets expire after 120 hours (five days). Expiration is not proof
  of destruction and does not reclaim a remaining balance.
- Keep a clean, approachable mobile-wallet UI rather than an engineering console.
- Track real prices and market drops, not simulated prices or market manipulation.
- Keep this roadmap current when files are added, changed, renamed or removed.

# Architecture and trust boundaries

```text
Owner browser (HTTPS)
  -> Coolify website: React static assets + Express API
      -> Cloudflare D1: application metadata
      -> private vault-engine:9090 (matching service token)
          -> Bitcoin Core RPC (private network + cookie authentication)
          -> persistent signer journal and Core wallet storage
      -> optional market Worker (not currently established as live)

Optional health replication:
  signer -> authenticated HTTPS Worker -> bounded metadata replication
Optional encrypted recovery exports:
  operator-controlled offline tooling -> encrypted backup storage
```

The browser does not hold Core RPC credentials. In external custody mode, public
cold descriptors identify receiving destinations but do not authorize cold spending.
In opt-in server custody mode, a separate Main vault also holds signing keys in
Core. Main, spending and temporary keys belong to the Core/signer custody boundary.
D1 availability must not become the authority for Bitcoin signing correctness.
Never run two active signers against the same state.

## Repository structure

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `artifacts/bitcoin-vault/` | Live React/Vite wallet UI and public HTML generators |
| `artifacts/api-server/` | Express API, authentication, passkeys, metadata, market and mail adapters |
| `artifacts/mockup-sandbox/` | Separate visual prototype workspace; not the production wallet |
| `services/vault-engine/` | Go engine, Core RPC, wallets, payment journal, reconciliation and tests |
| `lib/api-spec/` | Authoritative OpenAPI contract and Orval generation configuration |
| `lib/api-client-react/` | Generated client/hooks plus custom fetch/session handling |
| `lib/api-zod/` | Generated API validation schemas/types |
| `lib/vault-cloudflare/` | Worker, D1 migration, price and replication implementation |
| `lib/db/` | Unused PostgreSQL starter; do not migrate the vault into it |
| `deploy/` | Coolify, Core and signer container/operating configuration |
| `scripts/` | Verification, packaging, offline backup, generator and release utilities |
| `docs/` | Detailed runbooks and historical readiness records |
| `attached_assets/` | Uploaded reference images/text/logs; not application runtime dependencies |
| `.agents/memory/` | Project decisions and environment lessons, not credentials |
| `generated-artifacts/` | Excluded generated exports; not authoritative source |

## Authentication and sessions

The lock page accepts a saved keyfile or pasted owner key. The server verifies
the credential against its verifier; the owner secret must not be placed in
source code, chat or this document. Passkey enrollment and login use WebAuthn.
Session handling includes origin/CSRF protections, expiration, revocation,
rate-limiting and security notification support. Logout clears protected client
state and handles an already-expired session as logged out.

**Owner-confirmed on 2026-10-14:** passkey sign-in is working on the deployed app.
This confirms the reported sign-in experience, not every enrollment, revocation,
cross-device or recovery scenario.

Changing the deployment origin can affect cookies and WebAuthn. Preserve a working
owner-key backup and verify origin/RP configuration before changing domains.

## Dashboard, receiving and temporary wallets

The overview polls balances and node readiness. Missing node data must not appear
as a fabricated balance. Wallet pages expose receipt, labels, details and batch
creation. The receive interface uses the server's receive result, QR encoding,
copy/share controls and network warnings.

Signet native SegWit addresses begin with `tb1`, but this prefix alone does not
uniquely distinguish Signet from all other Bitcoin test networks. The configured
node network is authoritative. Real Bitcoin mainnet must not be sent to the
current QR codes.

Creation is blocked while Core reports initial block download or blocks trail
headers. The current “disconnected” presentation can also mean reconciliation is
incomplete; it must not be mistaken for proof that network transport is broken.
After sync the engine attempts initialization/reconciliation of the cold and
spending wallets. Temporary wallets are independent from those two main wallets.

## Sending, sweeping and recovery

Payments have review/approval and durable transaction tracking. Signed transaction
identity is journaled before broadcast so ambiguous responses can be reconciled
instead of blindly creating a second payment. Replacement, eviction, conflict
and reorg handling are separate from “success”.

Temporary sweeps require at least three confirmations and fresh cold destinations.
Three confirmations reduce risk; they are not an absolute finality guarantee.
Legacy cold spending requires signing outside this web application. Server-held
Main and Spending wallets can both be selected as payment sources in the Send UI.
The review pins the source wallet; approval and fee replacement use that source.

Sweeps default to paused and limits default to zero. Configure suitable positive
fee and exposure limits before deliberately enabling operations. Fee estimates
that are missing or exceed limits must not silently authorize a payment.

## Expiry and destruction

At five days, a temporary wallet is expired, not magically erased. The implementation
retains keys while funds, unsettled transactions or uncertainty remain. Actual key
destruction/history removal remains blocked because secure storage erasure has not
been verified. Manual deletion must not bypass those conditions.

Deleting local records does not remove public blockchain transactions. Core unload,
file deletion and volume deletion are not proof that copies disappeared from SSD,
snapshots, swap, journals or backups. A retained shared seed must not silently
regenerate supposedly destroyed wallets. Late deposits to old addresses remain
possible; there is no guaranteed maximum confirmation delay.

## Market and notifications

The Worker implements Kraken XBTUSD sampling and D1 price history, with freshness
checks and price-drop alerts. The latest dashboard screenshot shows the market
service disconnected. Verify provider terms and Worker configuration before
enabling market ingestion. Do not invent prices.

Mail/security-alert code and configuration are present; deployed delivery must be
verified separately. Do not infer working mail from a successful website build.

# Storage, backups and privacy

| Store | Purpose | Operational boundary |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Vault application metadata; migration includes `vault_state`, `prices`, `replica` | Production must not silently fall back to local SQLite |
| Development SQLite | Local metadata adapter | Not the deployed D1 database |
| Core data volume | Blockchain and wallet data | Persistent; do not delete to troubleshoot routine deployment errors |
| Signer volume | Durable state, payment intent and recovery information | Single-writer authority; protect against rollback |
| Core cookie volume | Local RPC authentication | Read-only in signer; never expose publicly |
| R2 / replication scaffolding | Encrypted backup destination / bounded health metadata | Live restoration and end-to-end binding checks remain pending |

The offline backup utility uses AES-256-GCM with an independent 32-byte backup
key. That key is not the owner login key or signer service token. Recovery exports
must exclude temporary wallets and the whole hot-wallet journal. An opaque
spending/reserve-wallet backup cannot be proven safe merely by validating its JSON
wrapper. Recovery JSON now permits `reserveWalletBackupBase64` for the permanent
Main vault; this does not authorize backing up temporary wallets.

Health replication is a bounded snapshot channel, not a complete audit trail:
intermediate health samples may be coalesced. Do not claim that its queue contains
wallet payment history or that it is a substitute for recovery backups.

# Deployment and configuration

## Website resource

Root `Dockerfile` builds the API and React app, then runs a non-root Node 24
container on port 3000. Its health check calls `/api/healthz`. Coolify routes the
public HTTPS website to this resource. Static files are served before SPA fallback.

Runtime configuration includes these **names only**:

- `NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, `BITCOIN_NETWORK`, `VAULT_STATIC_DIR`.
- `VAULT_OWNER_VERIFIER` — verifier only, never the raw owner credential.
- `VAULT_ENGINE_URL`, `VAULT_ENGINE_TOKEN` — private signer access.
- `CF_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CF_D1_DATABASE_ID`, `CF_API_TOKEN` — D1 access.
- `MARKET_WORKER_URL` — optional configured market service.
- `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`,
  `SECURITY_ALERT_FROM`, `SECURITY_ALERT_TO`, `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` — mail/proxy configuration.

`deploy/app-config.mjs` and the environment examples remain authoritative for exact
validation requirements. Do not copy real values into documentation.

## Separate Bitcoin stack

- Build pack: Docker Compose; branch: `main`; base directory: `/`.
- Compose file: `/deploy/coolify-bitcoin.compose.yaml`.
- Coolify resolves build contexts from the repository root through
  `--project-directory`; both build contexts must follow that convention.
- Core and signer run on the same host as the website with private networking.
- Owner screenshot established shared network `coolify`; verify again if moving hosts.
- Core uses an internal RPC network and an outbound peer network.
- Signer additionally joins the existing application network.
- No public domains or host port mappings for Core RPC or signer.
- Required Compose runtime input names: `VAULT_ENGINE_TOKEN`, `COOLIFY_NETWORK`.
  `VAULT_CUSTODY_MODE` defaults to `external` for compatibility. External cold
  receiving/sweeping needs `COLD_DESCRIPTOR` and `COLD_DESCRIPTOR_SHA256`;
  server-held custody uses `VAULT_CUSTODY_MODE=server` without an external descriptor.
- Existing website uses `VAULT_ENGINE_URL=http://vault-engine:9090` on the verified
  shared private network and the same signer token.
- Disable build-time availability for signer credentials. Do not bake them into images.
- Core's Compose health check stays enabled. Do not add an unauthenticated HTTP
  check to the signer's protected `/status` endpoint.
- “Healthy” means the health probe passed; it does not mean initial sync finished.

Core is pinned to 29.0 for the current test deployment with a tarball checksum.
Reassess maintenance/security versions before any mainnet deployment; a checksum
check is not a claim of an independent release-signature verification.

## Setup generators

`public/offline-keygen.html` is for owner credentials. The Signet generator's source
is in `scripts/signet-setup-generator.mjs` plus its HTML template; the build script
produces `public/signet-setup.html` and an excluded downloadable copy.

The owner chose HTTPS on-device generation for a disposable Signet wallet because
the phone's downloaded-file preview did not run it. The page generates locally,
requires saving a private backup before showing deployment variables, and is not
a mainnet cold-wallet ceremony. The temporary homepage buttons were removed after
the owner obtained the setup. The HTML file remains present.

## Release and rollback discipline

Validate first, inspect changes, fetch GitHub, preserve existing history and use a
normal fast-forward push. Do not force-push or expose deploy private keys. A push is
not proof of a successful Coolify rollout. Observe runtime logs after deployment.
Never remove persistent wallet volumes as a casual rollback strategy.

xvda1=98.9G ext4 mounted at /. Final df shows root=96G, used=16G, available=81G.
Partition/filesystem expansion is complete; no further resize command is needed.

Still open: secure HTTPS management access, the Coolify browser terminal failure,
encrypted mainnet storage/backups, host updates/restart planning, memory headroom,
the separate mainnet deployment/sync, live R2 restoration and controlled real-BTC
receive/send. SSH through the owner's CloudShell session worked; the browser
terminal did not. No credentials were shared and no hosted mainnet switch occurred.

## Commissioning preparation and access boundary — 2026-10-15

Protected routes now load on demand with Suspense inside the existing route
error boundary. The production initial JS chunk decreased from about 965 kB to
460 kB (146 kB gzip); the market route is separate at 396 kB. No emitted chunk
exceeds the default 500 kB warning threshold. Build/typecheck and standalone
packaging checks passed. This does not constitute authenticated mobile verification.

Found and closed a Worker recovery-interface gap: authenticated GET of an
allowlisted `.vault` backup now retrieves encrypted R2 bytes, with no-store,
attachment/nosniff headers, size bounds and explicit missing/outage responses.
No decryption keys enter the Worker and no live wallet is overwritten. Unit tests
cover authorization, exact bytes, missing objects, invalid paths and R2 failures.
Live deployment/object restoration has not been performed.

Session-lock regression and queue sequencing/durable-acknowledgement/retry tests
passed again. Source inspection and fixtures are not proof of live queue health.
No secure Coolify management endpoint/token is configured in this workspace.
Hosted sync, authenticated browser access, isolated live backup restore and
bounded production load measurement need operator access and agreed targets.
Real-BTC transfers require separately confirmed amounts, fees and destinations.
No funds moved, production credentials changed, or live restore/load test executed.

## Pre-redeploy verification — 2026-10-15

Workspace and Cloudflare typechecks passed. API/admission, static routing,
session-lock, ledger identity, delay rules, Compose/configuration, backup,
Cloudflare replica, generator/browser, package/runtime and live-probe unit tests
passed. API and frontend production builds completed; frontend reports a
roughly 965 kB uncompressed JS bundle and source-map warnings. These remain
performance/tooling follow-ups, not build failures.

The verification pass found and corrected two outdated test expectations:
production setup HTML must return 404, and disposable owner login fixtures must
use 64 bytes, not the former 164-byte format. Real credentials were untouched.

App and signer linux/amd64 images built. Isolated smoke tests validate non-root
configuration, static/SPA routing, authenticated disposable-key login, unauthorized
rejection and disconnected Signet behavior; no host ports or external network used.
Full Core regtest with race detection and Go vet passed, including custody,
confirmation progression, duplicate sends, replacement and recovery scenarios.

GitHub main was fetched successfully using the configured deploy identity; there
were no remote-only commits at verification. No force-push or deployment was
performed. The private deploy-key file is ignored by Git. This is not a full
security audit or a guarantee that no secret exists anywhere in repository history.

Source/build readiness is distinct from commissioning: hosted mainnet sync,
real-BTC round trip, live R2 restore,
authenticated mobile UX checks and production capacity measurements remain open.

## Transfer delay signals — 2026-10-15

History now shows elapsed-time signals on mobile cards and in the desktop table.
Browser-local warning thresholds are 30, 60 (default), or 120 minutes from first
seen while fewer than three confirmations are reported. It is not time since the
latest block or an estimated completion time. Signals update on a 15-second
clock; paused views evaluate against the frozen snapshot timestamp.
Completed, replaced, conflicted, failed/expired/abandoned and unknown broadcast
states are distinguished rather than labeled as ordinary delays. Invalid/future
timestamps report unavailable timing. Stale data can yield stale signals.

Threshold rules have unit coverage for boundaries, confirmations/reorgs,
exceptional states and timestamps. This is display-only: no fee change, automatic
retry, push notification or diagnosed root cause. Possible network causes are
explicitly described as possibilities, not facts. Configuration persistence
failures are shown and never silently claimed successful.

## History organization and mobile stability — 2026-10-15

Transaction history now renders paginated cards below the desktop breakpoint
and retains the desktop table. Mobile controls have larger touch targets; tables
without card renderers scroll within their own container. Search text and sort
values are indexed/memoized rather than repeatedly computed inside comparators.
Search, sort, page-size and external filter changes reset pagination.

Pause updates freezes a displayed snapshot and disables polling/focus/reconnect
fetches for that observer; manual refresh explicitly replaces the snapshot.
Resume returns to live 15-second polling. Stale/error indicators and the
three-confirmation meaning remain visible.

Row identity now distinguishes txid, wallet, direction, address and amount; truly
identical entries get occurrence suffixes instead of being dropped. Source output
indices are not exposed by the API, so identical-entry ordinal stability still
depends on server ordering. Three identity unit tests and frontend typecheck pass.

Limits: client-side pagination still downloads the server result; Core history
scans are not server-paginated, and these UI changes do not prove lag-free
large-history behavior. Authenticated mobile browser verification remains pending.

## Incoming confirmation audit — 2026-10-15

Extended the real Core regtest to assert incoming history at each confirmation:
0 = pending, 1–2 = confirming, 3 = confirmed. The test passed alongside its
existing duplicate-send, fee-replacement and reorg assertions.
History now displays Unconfirmed / Processing / Complete with 0–3 progress,
actual totals above three, 15-second polling and an explicit stale-update warning.
“Complete” is the application's three-confirmation threshold, not irreversible
finality. This remains local evidence, not hosted mainnet receipt verification.

Outgoing fee control is currently manual sat/vB plus reviewed RBF replacement.
Fast/Slow fee presets and token exchange are not implemented and must not be
presented as working. Exchange/provider scope needs separate clarification.

## Mainnet configuration and burst handling — 2026-10-15

Source now supports exact network `main` with `ALLOW_MAINNET=true` on the website
and signer. Mainnet requires server custody and separate network-pinned journal
storage. A separate Compose resource and private hostname preserve Signet volumes.
Mainnet Core 29.4 was built and started at genesis with networking disabled;
this is packaging evidence, not sync or payment readiness.

Added bounded API/signer admission and in-flight-only read coalescing without
persistent caches. A local 10,000-request HTTP fixture at concurrency 256 produced
8,829 successes and 1,171 explicit overload responses, peak admission 128,
117 upstream fixture reads, 13,974 ms total and 423 ms combined p95 latency.
These figures do not establish production throughput, D1 capacity or Bitcoin TPS.
The signer retains one signing authority and rejects overload rather than creating
unbounded signing work.

Index/SPA pages remain available; crawler exclusion metadata/headers are added.
Production setup-generator pages are denied and excluded from the runtime image.
No private keys are embedded in public HTML. Noindex is not access control.

Actual mainnet deployment, hosted recovery,
real-Bitcoin round trip, R2 restore and host load measurement remain pending.
See `docs/mainnet-and-capacity.md` for measurements, limits and operator steps.

The owner reconfirmed single-owner scope. Implemented opt-in server-held Main

destinations, source labels, and reserve backup-envelope support.
Existing external/watch-only mode remains the default. Mode changes require paused

Local evidence: Go race/regtest suite and vet passed. Additional isolated Core

The actual automatic sweep estimator path and all hosted custody flows still need

These changes are workspace implementation, not evidence of a Coolify rollout,

# Roadmap and acceptance criteria

## Owner's current release order

The owner has now requested the mainnet/production transition. Real Bitcoin
receiving and sending are the immediate goal; this is authorization to prepare
that transition, not evidence that mainnet is enabled or verified.
Keep this phase focused without adding unrelated access friction. Retain essential
network, authentication, transaction-integrity and readiness safeguards.

A public API with rate limiting is explicitly deferred until the owner has
confirmed real-Bitcoin receiving and sending work. The owner will explain its
operating model later. Do not expose the private signer or Core RPC as that API.
**Custody clarification — 2026-10-15:** The owner wants the vault itself to hold
spendable keys, receive and send using its own Bitcoin Core infrastructure,
support multiple wallets/transfers and track failed/incomplete transfers for
recovery. An external wallet address is not a prerequisite. This supersedes the
earlier Trust Wallet fixed-destination choice; do not implement that superseded
direction merely because it was previously approved.

The target is a server-held main/reserve wallet, spending wallet and independent
temporary receiving wallets. These are online/hot custody, not offline cold
storage. The existing deployed watch-only cold wallet is not this new target.
The first opt-in implementation is now present in the workspace and locally
validated; hosted migration and mainnet remain pending. Do not overwrite wallet state
silently; separate mainnet storage and preserve the current Signet environment.

“Multiple threads” means concurrent wallet activity with coordinated coin selection
and signing, not uncontrolled parallel spending of the same UTXOs. Transaction
utilities must distinguish pending, confirmed, failed, unknown broadcast, evicted,
replaced and conflicted states as applicable. Reconcile known signed transactions
before retrying; fee increases need controlled review. Recovery cannot reverse a
confirmed payment, guarantee mining, or restore destroyed private keys.

## 1. Finish hosted Signet commissioning

- Demonstrate temporary-wallet creation and persistence across a controlled restart.
- Receive test coins and show pending -> confirmed transitions from this node.
- Review/send once, confirm on-chain, and demonstrate safe duplicate handling.
- Configure positive fee/exposure limits deliberately; exercise sweeps at three
  confirmations and confirm destination/accounting.
- Exercise unavailable-node behavior, recovery and restored-wallet reconciliation
  with disposable test funds and preserved backups.
- Retain passkey owner confirmation; separately verify revocation, expiry,
  logout across tabs and account-recovery paths if those behaviors change.
- Improve status labels so transport connectivity and wallet readiness are distinct.

## 2. Finish external services and recovery evidence

- Commission market Worker only after provider/configuration approval.
- Verify alert delivery and clear failure reporting.
- Verify live D1/R2/Worker/replication bindings, authentication and outage replay.
- Perform an actual encrypted recovery round trip and restore reconciliation.

## 3. Mainnet migration — explicit separate release

- Review custody/security assumptions and maintained dependency/Core versions.
- Introduce consistent mainnet configuration across API, signer, UI and validators.
- Provision separate mainnet storage and server-held main/reserve and spending
  wallets, with independent temporary wallets and verified recovery backups.
- Replace the mandatory external cold-descriptor dependency for this custody mode;
  accurately label server-held reserves as online custody.
- Never reuse the disposable web-generated Signet private backup for mainnet custody.
- Synchronize mainnet and validate readiness; do not bypass syncing gates.
- Verify small controlled receive/send/recovery behavior before meaningful funds.
- Keep clear network labels and QR validation; changing wording is not migration.

## 4. Destruction policy implementation

Retain disabled destruction until an approved independent key lifecycle and copy
inventory can support verifiable erasure. Define late-deposit handling and irreversible
loss consequences. Blockchain history cannot be erased by this application.

# Developer workflow and verification

```sh
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm --filter @workspace/api-spec run codegen
bash scripts/vault-verify.sh
node scripts/build-signet-generator.mjs
node scripts/update-roadmap.mjs
node scripts/update-roadmap.mjs --check
```

Run codegen only when changing the API contract, and rebuild the Signet HTML after
editing its generator/template. The broad verification script covers types,
Node/API/frontend utility tests, deployment packaging and Go checks. Inspect its
current contents for the exact suite. Regtest and container probes are local
evidence, not replacements for hosted commissioning.

Documentation-only work should validate documentation/inventory, not unnecessarily
restart services or run real payment flows. No new live-payment evidence is claimed
by this roadmap update.

# Continuous documentation contract

For every codebase update:

1. Update the relevant narrative sections, status evidence, configuration and tests.
2. Refresh the inventory with `node scripts/update-roadmap.mjs`.
3. Review its added/changed/removed list. Confirm that exclusions are intentional.
4. Run `node scripts/update-roadmap.mjs --check` before release.
5. Keep pending work pending until evidence supports completion.

The script enumerates tracked plus non-ignored untracked project files, excludes
private/tool-generated locations, and records file size and SHA-256 content
fingerprints. The document's own fingerprint normalizes the generated inventory
section to avoid a self-referential hash. Changes to the narrative are still detected.
This is an inventory freshness check, not an automatic semantic code reviewer.
Purpose summaries are indexed roles, not a claim that every line was manually audited.

Never inventory actual secrets, `.env` values, private keys, wallet backups, database
contents, installed dependencies or local tool state. Uploaded evidence is listed
by filename only; its text/images are not copied into the roadmap.

## Excluded file classes

`.git`, `.local`, `.cache`, `.config`, `node_modules`, build output, caches, generated
exports, temporary logs, secret files and wallet/database state are excluded.
Tracked source-generated clients and the public bundled Signet page remain included.
Ignored uploads are outside the version-controlled handoff; tracked uploads remain
listed as evidence assets. Filenames are not evidence that an attachment is safe
to publish: review repository assets before release.
